title: KV offload thresholds and graceful degradation notes
content:
Purpose and scope

Quick note: this is an operationally focused sketch for how the runtime should decide to offload KV pages to host (PCIe) vs keep resident on GPU/UMA, and how to fail gracefully when host paging becomes the cause of latency SLO violations. Not a final spec — more of a playbook + experiment matrix.

Goals
- Keep P95 token latency within configured SLOs while minimizing GPU memory footprint and total cost.
- Avoid pathological host-paging storms that spike tail latency.
- Provide clear degraded modes and observable signals so Console/ops can set policies per-tenant.

Assumptions and constraints
- Hardware: machines with discrete GPU + host DRAM (PCIe link) and UMA nodes (NvLink/CCIX type shared memory) both in fleet.
- KV cache stores per-token KV slices; hotness is skewed across request types (some prompts have heavy reuse).
- We already have continuous-batching and per-request latency budgets. Offload decisions must be cheap (no per-token ML controller for now).

High-level idea
- Maintain a small resident working set on GPU. Cold KV pages are candidates for offload to host.
- Use multi-signal thresholds (resident utilization, pcie-occupancy, host-fault-rate, on-host-LRU-age) to decide transitions.
- Graceful degradation path: when host paging causes SLO risk, throttle new requests, expand batching windows (if client latency tolerance allows), or fall back to smaller model variant.

Signals we need (observable and in-memory counters):
- gpu_kv_bytes_in_use (per model-instance)
- gpu_free_bytes
- host_kv_bytes_used (on-node)
- pcie_transfer_in_flight (bytes)
- pcie_queue_latency_ms (quantile)
- host_page_faults_per_minute (per host slab region)
- kv_prefetch_hit_ratio (prefetch effectiveness)
- request_tail_latency_percentiles (P50/P95/P99)
- offload_eviction_rate (items/sec)
- prefetch_fill_time_ms (time to bring page back to GPU)

Decision surface (rule-based controller)
1) Immediate eviction path: when gpu_kv_bytes_in_use > target_resident_bytes then pick victim pages by recency + estimated reaccess probability and enqueue host-write. target_resident_bytes is calibrated per model size and SLA tier.

2) PCIe safety clamp: if pcie_transfer_in_flight > pcie_max_in_flight_bytes or pcie_queue_latency_ms > pcie_latency_threshold_ms, stop issuing non-urgent offloads (defer to next lower pressure tick). This prevents saturating link during bursts.

3) Host paging backpressure: if host_page_faults_per_minute spikes > host_fault_threshold OR prefetch_hit_ratio < min_prefetch_hit, then switch to conservative mode:
   - Reduce target_resident_bytes by small delta (to force fewer evicts)
   - Increase prefetch aggressiveness for pages with very high reuse probability
   - Temporarily disable background bulk-evictions (only evict at request-time when safe)

4) SLA-aware failover: if request_tail_latency_percentiles (P95) creeps above configured_slo * 0.95 for 30s AND host_page_faults_per_minute is elevated, trigger one of (policy selects):
   - route requests to dedicated capacity (if available)
   - fall back to quantized / smaller model variant for that tenant
   - enable local low-latency cache for critical tokens (sticky cache)
   - throttle low-priority requests (best-effort queueing)

Threshold defaults (initial proposal — to tune with experiments)
- target_resident_bytes: 60% of model_kv_footprint for prod-regular tier; 80% for high-tier SLA; 40% for best-effort workloads.
- pcie_max_in_flight_bytes: 8 GiB per-GPU (adjust per hw gen), burstable to 12 GiB with cooldown.
- pcie_latency_threshold_ms: 20 ms median queue latency; 50 ms 95th.
- host_fault_threshold: 200 faults/min per host slab region (tuned by footprint & host RAM).
- min_prefetch_hit: 0.6 (if < 60% prefetch hits, we re-evaluate policy).

Eviction selector heuristic
- Score(page) = alpha * recency_score + beta * size_penalty + gamma * reuse_score_estimate
- Prefer evicting large contiguous pages that are unlikely to be reused soon.
- Do not evict pages referenced in last N tokens (configurable N=4) unless under emergency memory pressure.

Prefetch strategy
- On request-access miss, synchronously try a fast on-demand fetch to GPU if prefetch_fill_time_ms < sync_fill_threshold (e.g., 5 ms). Otherwise schedule async prefetch.
- Background prefetcher maintains a small pipeline: identify top-M candidates from LRU and recent traces, prefetch when pcie utilization low.
- Conservative prefetching for UMA nodes: treat UMA reads as cheaper but contended; still prefer GPU residency for hot slices.

Graceful slowdown modes (ordered by intrusiveness)
- Mode 0 (Normal): aggressive eviction + background prefetching allowed.
- Mode 1 (Soft backpressure): suspend background bulk evictions; only evict at admission time; increase resident target slightly.
- Mode 2 (Throttled): pause non-critical offloads; compact cache aggressively for high-SLA tenants; prioritize prefetch for critical tokens.
- Mode 3 (Failover): route to fallbacks (smaller model, reserved capacity); surface incidents.

Operational playbook (runbook steps):
- Alert triggers: P95 latency > SLO*0.95 AND pcie_queue_latency_ms > pcie_latency_threshold_ms for 2 consecutive minutes.
- Initial action: flip node to Mode 1, increase per-tenant resident target by 5–10%.
- If no improvement in 3 minutes: escalate to Mode 2 and identify heavy offload sources (tenants with highest offload_eviction_rate).
- If sustained (>10 minutes) and customer impact: remind Console to engage route-to-dedicated/backfill policies and notify SRE.

Experiments to run (A/B matrix)
- Vary target_resident_bytes = {40, 60, 80}% across similar workload slices; measure P95, cost per token, offload bytes/sec.
- Test PCIe clamp tuning: pcie_max_in_flight_bytes = {4, 8, 12} GiB while under synthetic bursty workloads. Measure pcie queue latency and tail latency impact.
- Prefetch aggressiveness sweep: prefetch_candidates = {4, 16, 64} pages, and prefetch_rate_limit = {1GB/s, 2GB/s}. Track prefetch_hit_ratio and wasted bandwidth.
- UMA vs PCIe baseline: run on UMA node with identical workload and compare average prefetch_fill_time_ms and host_page_fault rates.

Metrics to capture for each experiment
- cost_per_token, p95_latency, p99_latency, offload_bytes_per_minute, prefetch_hit_ratio, pcie_queue_latency_ms, host_page_faults_per_minute, model_throughput_rps

Telemetry and Console UX
- Expose per-tenant "offload pressure" score (0..100) derived from normalized signals. Use this in Console to set per-tenant policy (aggressive, balanced, conservative).
- Provide time-series: resident_bytes, host_bytes, pcie_inflight, pcie_latency, offload_rate, prefetch_hit_ratio, latency_percentiles.
- Rate-limited historical traces for incidents with full kernel timestamps (to debug microbursts).

Open questions / TODOs
- How to safely estimate reuse_score_estimate in a streaming fashion without expensive counters? (Ideas: lightweight sampling, bloom filters of recent tokens).
- Should we implement per-tenant sticky pinning for top-K hot pages? Complexity vs benefit to be evaluated.
- Formalize interaction with autoscaler: autoscaler must be KV-aware (scale up when sustained offload pressure persists).
- Hardware-aware defaults: gather fleet telemetry per GPU generation and auto-calibrate pcie_max_in_flight_bytes.

Rollout plan
- Stage 1: implement signals + rule-based controller in canary cluster; run in monitor-only mode for 2 weeks and collect telemetry.
- Stage 2: enable conservative Mode 1 enforcement for non-prod workloads for 1 week.
- Stage 3: open beta for 10% of prod traffic with Mode 2 enabled; run experiments and collect cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Stage 4: GA with tenant-level policy knobs in Console.

Appendix: rough pseudocode for offload decision tick
- on memory_pressure_tick():
    if gpu_kv_bytes_in_use <= target_resident_bytes: return
    if pcie_transfer_in_flight > pcie_max_in_flight_bytes or pcie_queue_latency_ms > pcie_latency_threshold_ms:
        defer non_urgent_evictions()
        return
    for victim in select_victims():
        if host_page_faults_per_minute > host_fault_threshold and not victim.is_rarely_used():
            continue
        enqueue_offload(victim)

Notes to reviewers
- Please comment especially on: sensible defaults for pcie_max_in_flight_bytes for Ampere vs Hopper vs next-gen; how aggressive we should be with prefetch for small vs large token workloads; and any risks around per-tenant pinning.
- I'm intentionally leaving reuse_score_estimate fuzzy — want ops/telemetry to propose lightweight signals we currently collect that can be repurposed.

End of doc.
